title: How a Business Works
outcome: Map business functions; distinguish revenue, profit and cash; complete the baseline assessment.
evidence: Business process map and cash analysis
case: Vayentra Labs sells business support services. During September it earns INR 100,000 and incurs INR 75,000 of expenses. Customers pay INR 60,000; cash paid for expenses is INR 70,000. Opening bank is INR 20,000. No other cash flows occur. A manager says the INR 25,000 profit is available to spend.
concept: Revenue records earned services; receipts record cash collected. Profit is revenue less recognised expenses. Closing cash follows actual receipts and payments. A process handoff needs an owner, evidence and a control.
example: A separate job earns INR 8,000 on credit and incurs INR 3,000 paid costs. Profit is INR 5,000 but its immediate cash movement is negative INR 3,000.
task: Calculate September profit, net cash movement and closing cash. Draw enquiry to order to delivery evidence to invoice to collection. Identify three handoff failures and who should prevent them.
squad: Assign sales, delivery, finance and review roles. Finance has 60 seconds to answer whether a new INR 15,000 payment can be made while retaining a minimum INR 5,000 bank balance.
extras: Your faculty member issues a separate 60-minute baseline assessment before teaching. Complete it independently without AI or peer help. The baseline is diagnostic.
ai: Using only the supplied September case, create two separate schedules: profit and cash movement. Show each formula and label earned revenue versus cash receipts. Do not assume collections or financing that are not stated. Finish with the payment reserve test.
stretch: What changes if INR 20,000 is collected early but the customer receives a 2% discount? State the cash and margin tradeoff without assuming the customer agrees.

title: Professional Identity and Teamwork
outcome: Develop professional introductions, assign squad roles and establish accountability and work standards.
case: You join a five-person squad. Two students share one laptop; one travels 90 minutes; a reviewer is absent on the submission day. The manager requires a usable file by 18:00 the submission day and a status update before any deadline is missed.
concept: Accountability means one owner accepts a deliverable and confirms acceptance criteria. A reviewer checks work but does not erase ownership. Workload fairness is judged by attributable contributions, not speaking time.
example: A useful commitment reads: I own receipt matching, will submit the match log at 17:00, and will escalate missing reference numbers by 15:00.
task: Write a 90-second introduction linking your current skill to one entry-level task. Draft a charter specifying owner, reviewer, response window, file naming, escalation and a missed-deadline recovery rule.
squad: Allocate five roles: coordinator, finance, data, client communication and quality reviewer. Rotate each session; record the first four rotations. Negotiate a plan that gives each person 20 minutes of keyboard time.
ai: Review this squad charter for missing ownership, review, response windows, device-sharing arrangements and AI-use boundaries. Quote the relevant charter sentence for each observation. Suggest changes without inventing student availability.
stretch: Resolve a disagreement about whether the best Excel user should always operate the laptop. Preserve support while preventing dependency.

title: Workplace Communication
outcome: Write clarification emails, progress updates and professional escalation messages.
case: At 11:00 the manager writes: Send the best customers report today. You have invoice values but no collection records. The manager will choose customers for a credit-limit increase at 16:00. Revenue and payment reliability may point to different customers.
concept: A useful message states the decision, available evidence, missing information, proposed assumption and next update. Concision must not remove a material limitation. Never silently choose a metric that changes the decision.
example: Example subject: September debtor review - collection data needed by 14:00. First line: I can rank billed revenue now; I need payment dates to assess credit reliability.
task: Write a clarification email of 120 words maximum, a 40-word progress message and a 70-word escalation if payment data is unavailable at 14:00. Include an achievable next update.
squad: One student plays the manager and refuses a longer report. Negotiate a one-page output that separates revenue ranking from unverified credit-risk conclusions.
extras: Message received at 11:00: Send the best customers report today. Decision at 16:00: choose customers for a credit-limit increase. Payment history is unavailable. Use the facts in this brief; do not invent a customer list.
ai: Rewrite this clarification email in at most 120 words. Preserve all stated facts, uncertainty, deadlines and approval limits. Mark any fact you need as MISSING. Do not add promises or assume that high sales imply reliable payment.
stretch: Rewrite the same escalation for a time-poor CFO in 45 words while retaining the decision risk.

title: Meetings and Reporting
outcome: Run a structured meeting; document decisions, owners, deadlines and approval requirements.
case: A client delivery is due the agreed delivery day 17:00. A supplier expects to deliver the next day. A substitute can meet the agreed delivery day at INR 4,000 additional cost. The client has not accepted a changed deadline. The operations lead can approve up to INR 2,000; the manager is available at 15:00 today.
concept: Minutes capture decisions and unresolved decisions, not a transcript. Escalation moves a decision to the person with authority before the risk becomes irreversible. An option is not approved merely because a squad likes it.
example: Action record: Operations lead to confirm substitute availability by 14:30; manager to approve or reject INR 4,000 at 15:00; client lead to communicate the approved plan by 15:30.
task: Prepare a four-item agenda. Run a 12-minute meeting. Record two options, decision authority, action owners and deadlines. Deliver a 90-second done-next-blocker update.
squad: Rotate chair and minute-taker. Midway, the client asks for a guarantee. Answer without making an unauthorised promise. Launch Independent Practice 1 using the matching ticket.
extras: Meeting roles: operations lead explains the delay and authority limit; procurement presents the substitute; client lead protects the agreed commitment; manager decides whether to approve additional cost; minute-taker records unresolved decisions. Rotate roles.
ai: From this simulated meeting transcript, separate confirmed facts, proposed options, approved decisions and actions. Include owner and due time only when stated. Mark absent approval or ownership as unresolved and quote supporting lines.
stretch: Add a second supplier offering Friday delivery with no quality inspection. Explain what additional evidence is needed before choosing it.

practice.title: Communication under uncertainty
practice.brief: The substitute supplier now quotes INR 3,500 and can hold stock until 16:00. Operations approval limit remains INR 2,000. Manager review is 15:00; client delivery remains the agreed delivery day 17:00.
practice.output: Write a clarification/approval request of 120 words maximum, minutes with three owned actions and a 60-word status update. Acknowledge the ticket within your agreed availability window. Do not promise delivery before approval.
practice.rubric: Authority 3 points; owned actions and deadlines 3; clear concise writing 2; timely acknowledgement and evidence trail 2.

title: Accounting Transactions
outcome: Interpret source documents; classify transactions and prepare journal entries.
case: Use Case A in the data appendix. Twelve September events must be entered from source evidence. All values in this accounting-only case exclude indirect tax. No depreciation is required for this one-month exercise. Do not mix in the later GST case.
concept: Debits increase assets and expenses; credits increase liabilities, equity and revenue. Collection of an existing receivable does not create revenue again. A refundable advance is a liability until the service is earned.
example: A client pays an INR 8,000 existing invoice: debit Bank 8,000, credit Trade receivables 8,000. Revenue was recognised when the service was earned.
task: Create a transaction register with document ID, business event, debit account, credit account, amount and evidence status. Journal all 12 events. Flag the source needed for an accrued wage and a customer advance.
squad: Pair a preparer with a reviewer. Each student explains two entries without AI. The reviewer challenges why equipment is not treated as a current operating expense.

sources.title: Case A September accounting release
sources.description: Use in Sessions 5 and 6 only. Fictional Vayentra Labs business; INR; indirect tax omitted to isolate accounting. Opening balances on 1 September: Bank debit 100,000; Capital credit 100,000. Equipment is capitalised; depreciation is excluded for this teaching month. All transactions are supported by the described synthetic source records.
rows: Completed service on credit; client acceptance and invoice
Completed service paid immediately into bank
September software subscription paid by bank
September contractor service paid by bank
September wages earned but unpaid; approved wage schedule
Bank payment against A07 wage liability
Refundable customer advance received in bank; future service
Part of A09 advance refunded by bank
Bank charge shown on bank advice
Equipment bought and paid through bank

blocks.title: Evidence exceptions and classifications to explain

ai: Using Case A and this supplied chart of accounts, propose journal entries in columns source ID, debit, credit, amount and reason. Use REVIEW when a required document or policy is missing. Do not invent tax, depreciation or account codes.
stretch: Explain how a missing delivery acceptance record changes the review status of an invoice without automatically proving the sale is false.

title: Ledger and Month End Close
outcome: Post ledger entries, correct errors and prepare a trial balance and income statement.
case: Continue Case A. The draft ledger incorrectly records the INR 35,000 customer collection as new revenue. The bank posting is correct. Management asks you to close the month and explain whether an agreeing trial balance proves the accounts are accurate.
concept: A trial balance checks equality of debits and credits; balanced misclassifications can remain. Closing requires source completeness, accruals, liability checks and a reviewer. Corrections need an audit trail.
example: If a prior receivable collection is credited to revenue in error, reverse the excess revenue and credit receivables: Dr Revenue, Cr Trade receivables. Cash is unchanged.
task: Post Case A to ledgers. Correct the deliberate INR 35,000 error. Produce a closing trial balance, income statement and accounting equation check. State two errors a trial balance cannot detect.
squad: Conduct a close meeting: preparer explains the correction, reviewer checks the evidence, and manager signs only after bank, AR and liabilities are reviewed.

Opening balances on 1 September: Bank debit 100,000; Capital credit 100,000. Equipment is capitalised; depreciation is excluded for this teaching month. All transactions are supported by the described synthetic source records.

Bank payment against A07 wage liability
Refundable customer advance received in bank; future service
Part of A09 advance refunded by bank
Bank charge shown on bank advice

ai: Review this trial balance and correction log against Case A. Separate arithmetic agreement from evidence of classification and completeness. Identify the three accounts whose support you would inspect first and explain why. Do not state that balanced totals prove accuracy.
stretch: A supplier bill arrives after close for services received in September. Explain the period question and evidence needed before posting an accrual.

title: Excel and Data Cleaning
outcome: Preserve raw data; handle duplicates and missing values; apply formulas and validation checks.
case: Use Case B raw receipts. The file contains a repeated ID, an invalid date, an ambiguous date, a blank amount and inconsistent customer names. The manager asks for total receipts by customer.
concept: Preserve Raw, transform into Clean, and document Exceptions. Duplicate detection needs a business key and evidence. An error should be visible; replacing unknown amounts with zero creates misleading certainty.
example: For an Excel table named Clean, =SUMIFS(Clean[Amount],Clean[Customer],A2) totals an approved customer. =COUNTIF(Raw[ID],[@ID]) flags repeated IDs; it does not decide which row is valid.
task: Type Case B exactly as received into Raw. Define a date and customer standard; add row status and source ID. Quarantine unresolved rows, compute approved totals and add a control that counts excluded rows.
squad: One student cleans, another tries to reproduce the result from Raw and the log. Change one approved amount and show that the total updates. Save a formula view or formula text.

sources.title: Case B Raw receipt import
sources.description: Use in Session 7. Copy all seven rows exactly to Raw. Dates must ultimately be unambiguous ISO dates. The collection officer confirms the two R02 rows are a repeated export of one receipt. No clarification is available for R04, R05 or R06. Customer master: ASHA = Asha; BEACON = Beacon. Do not infer unknown data.

ai: Use a copy of Case B. Preserve Raw. Propose Clean and Exceptions tables with source row IDs and reasons. Do not resolve ambiguous dates or blank amounts by guessing. Suggest SUMIFS and duplicate-count formulas, explaining their assumptions before applying them.
stretch: Add a validation list for status and an exception count. Explain why formula correctness does not prove source data completeness.

title: Bank Reconciliation
outcome: Match book and bank records; separate timing differences from errors and record adjustments.
case: Case C October snapshot: unadjusted cash book INR 87,500 debit; bank statement INR 83,200 credit balance. Statement shows bank charge INR 500 and interest INR 200 absent from books. A customer deposit INR 10,000 is in books but not bank; a supplier payment INR 6,000 is in books but not yet debited by bank. No other differences exist.
concept: First update the books for genuine bank-only items. Then reconcile timing differences without recording them twice. State the starting perspective and sign convention. An unexplained plug is not a reconciliation.
example: In a separate example, adjusted book balance 20,000 plus an unpresented payment 3,000 less a deposit in transit 5,000 gives statement balance 18,000.
task: Calculate adjusted book bank, bridge it to the statement and show a zero difference. Draft the two journal entries. Create an exception log with source, owner and follow-up date.
squad: A reviewer asks you to post the INR 10,000 deposit again. Explain why that would be wrong. Start Independent Practice 2 with the independent variant.

blocks.title: Followup owner and source for timing items

ai: Build a reconciliation from Case C with separate book adjustments and timing differences. Show the starting perspective and signs. List the journal entries only for book adjustments. Leave unexplained differences visible; do not create balancing entries.
stretch: If the deposit remains absent after seven business days, specify evidence to obtain and an escalation threshold.

practice.title: Independent reconciliation
practice.brief: Books 52,000; bank statement 55,300. Bank fee 300 and interest 100 are absent from books. Unpresented payment 5,500; deposit in transit 2,000. No other differences.
practice.output: Prepare adjusted books, statement bridge, two journals and a two-item follow-up log. Include formula text or transparent arithmetic and a 60-word manager note.
practice.rubric: Adjusted books and bridge 4; journals 2; timing classification 2; reproducibility and status update 2.

title: Business Finance and Performance
outcome: Calculate growth and margins; interpret costs and receivables; distinguish facts from assumptions.
case: Use Case D three-month MIS. Revenue grows each month, but direct-cost intensity and receivables also rise. The owner says sales growth proves the business is healthier.
concept: Gross margin measures revenue after direct costs. Operating margin also deducts operating overhead. Percentage-point change differs from percentage growth. Receivables are a balance at a date, not automatically an expense or cash loss.
example: If revenue is 80,000 and direct cost 32,000, gross profit is 48,000 and gross margin 60%. A fall from 60% to 55% is 5 percentage points.
task: Calculate gross profit, operating profit, both margins for all months and September versus August revenue and profit growth. Write three findings, one uncertainty and one investigation.
squad: Finance defends the diagnosis to sales. Separate observed cost intensity from an unproven claim that discounting caused it.

sources.title: Case D Three month MIS release
sources.description: Use in Sessions 9, 10, 13 and 14. These monthly management snapshots are a separate teaching release from Case A and must not be combined with its ledger. All figures INR, net of tax. Direct costs and overheads are recognised expenses; receivables are closing balances. Collection dates and causes of cost changes are not supplied.

blocks.title: Revenue and operating profit growth calculations
Three findings with evidence and a limitation

ai: Using Case D only, calculate gross and operating profit and margins for each month. Separate observed changes from possible causes. State missing evidence before explaining causality. Keep units and percentage-point changes explicit.
stretch: Estimate what September operating profit would be at August gross margin with September revenue and overhead unchanged.

title: MIS Dashboard Development
outcome: Build an updating management information system dashboard and present decision-focused recommendations.
case: The owner has five minutes. Use Case D to build one page showing whether sales growth is converting to margin and what needs investigation. There is no collection ledger in this release.
concept: A dashboard begins with a decision. Label period, units, definitions and source. A KPI needs context and an owner; a decorative chart without a decision wastes attention. A memo states insight, evidence, action and limitation.
example: A decision-useful line reads: September revenue rose 25% over August, while operating margin fell from 22.5% to 20%; review direct-cost mix before adding sales targets.
task: Build an Excel dashboard with revenue trend, gross margin, operating margin and closing receivables. Add the calculation cells, source reference and a 150-word management memo with two actions.
squad: Give a three-minute management review. Reviewer changes September direct cost from 75,000 to 78,000 and tests whether all affected outputs update.

sources.title: Case D Three month MIS release
sources.description: Use in Sessions 9, 10, 13 and 14. These monthly management snapshots are a separate teaching release from Case A and must not be combined with its ledger. All figures INR, net of tax. Direct costs and overheads are recognised expenses; receivables are closing balances. Collection dates and causes of cost changes are not supplied.

blocks.title: Management memo with two owned actions

ai: Create a one-page MIS draft from Case D using revenue, gross margin, operating margin and receivables. Show the source cells and calculation logic. Specify how each chart and narrative will refresh. Do not invent targets or collection data.
stretch: Add a target margin input and flag variances. Explain why Power BI would be optional for this cohort rather than necessary to prove analysis.

title: GST and Invoice Review
outcome: Review classroom invoice cases, calculate supplied tax assumptions and reconcile purchase exceptions.
case: Use Case E only. For these domestic teaching cases, the approved trainer policy specifies 18% tax: intra-state 9% CGST plus 9% SGST; inter-state 18% IGST. Supplier location and place of supply are supplied. These assumptions do not establish the rate or treatment of a real service.
concept: Review invoice evidence before calculating. Customer address alone does not settle every place-of-supply question. Reconcile purchase records to the supplied inward statement; a match is evidence for review, not automatic permission to claim credit.
example: On taxable value 2,000 under the supplied intra-state policy, CGST is 180, SGST is 180 and invoice total is 2,360. Never apply each component at the full 18%.
task: Review all three sales invoices. Calculate correct tax components and totals; flag missing invoice number. Match P01-P03 to the supplied inward statement and identify the exception requiring follow-up.
squad: One student plays a supplier who says to claim all purchase tax now. Explain the evidence gap and route the unresolved item to the accounting mentor.

sources.title: Case E Invoice and inward statement review
sources.description: Use in Session 11. Synthetic domestic training policy: supplier location Karnataka; supplied place of supply determines the simplified case treatment. Taxable values are net of discounts. Assumed tax rate 18%; intra-state 9% plus 9%; inter-state 18%. No actual GSTINs, classifications or filing credentials are included. Real rates, place-of-supply rules and credit conditions require practitioner verification before any live adaptation.

sources.title: Purchase register and supplied inward statement
sources.description: Match by purchase ID. Record supported matches and exceptions. Do not infer eligible credit or tax payable.

blocks.title: Unresolved purchase item and mentor question

ai: Use only the supplied Case E policy and invoice records. Check invoice serial, taxable value, tax heads and totals. Cite the supplied rule for each exception. Separate arithmetic, missing evidence and policy questions. Do not introduce live tax rates or claim credit eligibility.
stretch: List what a practitioner must verify before applying this exercise to live transactions: current classification, place of supply, invoice rules and credit conditions.

title: Receivables and Working Capital
outcome: Prepare ageing schedules, prioritise collections and develop a short-term cash action plan.
case: Use Case F at 31 October. Four invoices total INR 100,000 outstanding. Bank is INR 25,000. Unavoidable payments due within seven days total INR 45,000. Beacon disputes INR 5,000 of its balance; none of the expected collections has cleared.
concept: Days overdue = max(0, as-of date minus due date). Current includes invoices due today. Separate amount from probability and promise from cash. A cash forecast should show confirmed and contingent receipts separately.
example: An invoice due 21 October is 10 days overdue on 31 October, even if it was issued a month earlier. Ageing uses the due date under this policy.
task: Prepare current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90 and over-90 buckets. Identify the minimum cash gap and a priority sequence. Draft a disputed-balance query and a payment reminder.
squad: Negotiate a cash plan with a supplier while the client disputes part of a bill. Record any proposed rescheduling as pending until the counterparty agrees. Launch Independent Practice 3.

sources.title: Case F Receivables and cash release
sources.description: Use in Sessions 12 and 17-20. As-of date 31 October 2026. Dates ISO; INR. Amounts are outstanding invoice totals, not taxable values. All invoices are unpaid. Bank 25,000; unavoidable seven-day outflows 45,000. Beacon disputes 5,000 within F02. No credit note has yet been approved in version 1. Contacts are role labels only.

sources.title: Purchase register and supplied inward statement
sources.description: Match by purchase ID. Record supported matches and exceptions. Do not infer eligible credit or tax payable.

ai: Using Case F as of 31 October, create ageing buckets from due dates and a seven-day cash scenario. Show confirmed and contingent amounts separately. Draft a respectful query for the disputed balance. Do not count the dispute twice or assume a promise is cleared cash.
stretch: If only INR 12,000 clears tomorrow, quantify the remaining gap and propose a documented escalation.

practice.title: Collection and tax exception
practice.brief: Use Case F version 1. Cedar pays INR 12,000 into bank on 1 November; no other payment or credit occurs. Update as of 1 November. Also draft the supplier query for missing P02 from Case E; do not calculate eligible credit.
practice.output: Update outstanding, ageing, bank and the original seven-day payment gap assuming the same 45,000 outflow window. Record the receipt allocation, collection message and P02 query.
practice.rubric: Updated balances and ageing 4; cash gap 2; correct exception handling 2; evidence and communication 2.

title: AI for Commerce Professionals
outcome: Prepare safe inputs and structured prompts for business analysis; document human review.
case: A colleague proposes pasting client names, bank details and Case D financial data into a public AI tool. Your task is to draft a management memo while keeping the original financial calculations under human control.
concept: Choose the task before the model. Minimise data, specify permitted sources and ask the tool to expose uncertainty. A fluent draft is not evidence of accuracy. Keep a manual route for calculations and review.
example: A safe task prompt can ask: Using only these approved monthly totals, draft 120 words on margin movement. Cite each figure by month. Do not infer causes or invent collection data. Mark missing evidence.
task: Create a data-minimisation plan, a prompt and an AI-use log. Use Case D only. If no AI tool is available, use the supplied flawed draft in Session 14 as the response to audit.
squad: One student prepares the input, another approves its data scope and a third verifies the resulting claims. Compare manual effort with assisted effort, recording actual minutes rather than estimating savings.

sources.title: Case D Three month MIS release
sources.description: Use in Sessions 9, 10, 13 and 14. These monthly management snapshots are a separate teaching release from Case A and must not be combined with its ledger. All figures INR, net of tax. Direct costs and overheads are recognised expenses; receivables are closing balances. Collection dates and causes of cost changes are not supplied.

extras: Offline AI draft to audit: September revenue grew 30%. Operating margin improved to 25%. All customers paid on time. Offer every customer a 20% discount to improve profitability. Treat every sentence as an unverified claim.
ai: Using only Case D, draft a 120-word management memo. Every numerical claim must identify the month and measure. Separate facts, possible explanations and missing evidence. Do not infer customer payment behaviour. Return a claim checklist for human review.
stretch: Design a test that compares two prompts on the same task using accuracy and review time, without assuming the longer prompt is better.

title: AI Verification and Automation
outcome: Audit generated claims against source data; test a controlled workflow and approval checkpoints.
evidence: Verified report and workflow test log
case: The AI draft says: September revenue grew 30%; operating margin improved to 25%; receivables of INR 70,000 prove customers paid on time. Offer 20% discounts to every customer. Audit this using Case D.
concept: A claim register connects each statement to a source, recalculation, verdict and correction. Automate repeatable checks; reserve judgement and external actions for approval. A workflow must stop visibly on invalid input.
example: For revenue growth, calculate (150,000 - 120,000) / 120,000 = 25%. Mark the 30% claim false and replace it; do not merely change its wording.
task: Audit all four claims. Write a corrected 120-word memo. Build a spreadsheet check that flags a missing month or nonnumeric revenue, and describe an input-review-draft-verify-approve workflow.
squad: Inject a blank revenue cell. The workflow must stop and flag missing input rather than produce a confident zero-growth statement. Reviewer signs the corrected memo.

sources.title: Case D Three month MIS release
sources.description: Use in Sessions 9, 10, 13 and 14. These monthly management snapshots are a separate teaching release from Case A and must not be combined with its ledger. All figures INR, net of tax. Direct costs and overheads are recognised expenses; receivables are closing balances. Collection dates and causes of cost changes are not supplied.

extras: Workflow test inputs: first use Case D unchanged. Then set September revenue to blank in a copy. The workflow must flag missing input and stop release. Restore the value; require a reviewer decision. Test rejection as well as approval.

blocks.title: Automation input test and approval condition

ai: Audit the supplied AI draft against Case D. For each claim, provide a source, calculation, verdict and correction. Then propose a workflow with validation, draft, human review and release stages. Do not send or publish anything.
stretch: Add a second test for negative revenue and explain when a genuine credit note should be reviewed rather than silently rejected.

title: Customer and Sales Operations
outcome: Maintain a customer relationship management tracker, analyse conversion and prioritise follow-up.
evidence: CRM tracker and sales funnel analysis
case: Use Case G eight unique leads. The period has three Won, two Lost and three Open leads. All contacts are fictional. Management wants a conversion rate and a next-action queue.
concept: A funnel is useful only with stable stage definitions and a known denominator. All-lead win rate differs from closed-lead win rate. Prioritise next actions using expressed need and due date, not personal characteristics.
example: With 2 wins from 10 leads, all-lead win rate is 20%; if only 4 are closed, closed-lead win rate is 50%. Both can be correct when labelled.
task: Create a CRM table with lead ID, stage, owner, next action and due date. Calculate both win rates. Find overdue open actions as of 31 October and draft two follow-up messages.
squad: A sales manager asks to label every Open lead as likely to close. Explain how pipeline uncertainty should be shown. Check whether two people have been assigned the same lead.

sources.title: Case G CRM release
sources.description: Use in Session 15 and capstone discovery. As-of date 31 October 2026. One row per distinct enquiry; no duplicates. Won and Lost are closed stages; Open remains undecided. Due dates refer to the next follow-up. There is no verified join key to Case F customers or invoices. Names below are fictional role owners.

blocks.title: All lead and closed lead win rates with denominators

ai: Using Case G, calculate all-lead and closed-lead win rates with explicit denominators. List overdue Open actions at the as-of date. Do not infer buying intent, demographic traits or invoice revenue from this tracker.
stretch: Design a response-time metric and explain why it cannot be calculated from this release without received and first-response timestamps.

title: Commercial Decision Making
outcome: Compare pricing and discount scenarios; calculate contribution, break-even and capacity effects.
case: An internal management-only scenario offers a service at net price INR 10,000, variable delivery cost INR 4,000 and fixed cohort cost INR 120,000. Demand is 25 seats; capacity is 30. A 10% discount may raise demand to 30. Ignore tax and collection timing for this scenario.
concept: Contribution per unit = net price minus variable cost. Break-even units = fixed costs / unit contribution, rounded up for whole units. Capacity limits can make a discount unable to improve profit.
example: At net price 5,000 and variable cost 2,000, contribution is 3,000; fixed cost 60,000 requires 20 units to break even.
task: Compare baseline 25 seats and discounted 30 seats. Calculate contribution, break-even seats and profit. Determine the minimum discounted seats to match baseline profit and whether the proposal should be approved.
squad: Sales argues that revenue growth is enough. Finance challenges the capacity and demand assumptions. Write a decision memo with a condition under which you would change your view. Launch Independent Practice 4.
ai: Compare the baseline and discount case using the supplied price, variable cost, fixed cost, expected demand and capacity. Show contribution, break-even and profit. Do not invent demand elasticity. Identify the capacity constraint and a downside scenario.
stretch: Quantify discounted profit at 28 seats and identify the maximum extra marketing spend if matching baseline profit is required.

practice.title: Discount sensitivity
practice.brief: Use Session 16 price, cost and capacity. Discounted demand reaches only 28 seats. Marketing proposes extra spend INR 6,000. Treat marketing as additional fixed cost.
practice.output: Calculate profit before and after extra marketing; compare with baseline 30,000 profit. State the capacity-constrained decision and a condition required before approval.
practice.rubric: Calculations and comparison 4; capacity logic 2; assumptions and decision 2; evidence and timely note 2.

title: Industry Challenge Discovery
outcome: Interview a client or simulated business owner; define the problem, evidence needs and success measures.
case: Use the Capstone Client Brief in the appendix. The founder reports slow cash visibility and asks for a dashboard. Data includes the Case F receivables and Case G leads, but there is no reliable join between leads and invoices.
concept: Discovery identifies the decision and process before the solution. A problem statement names user, problem, evidence, consequence and success measure. Keep client statements separate from measured facts.
example: Instead of We need AI, write: Finance needs a reviewed overdue-invoice queue because four accounts total INR 100,000 outstanding; our output must reconcile to that control total.
task: Prepare eight discovery questions and an interview record. State the problem in 80 words, list data permissions, and identify three assumptions that could invalidate the proposal.
squad: Facilitator plays client using the handbook answer card. Assign an interviewer and note-taker; every student asks at least one question. Choose the cash-control challenge or the equally scoped approved live project.

sources.title: Case F Receivables and cash release
sources.description: Use in Sessions 12 and 17-20. As-of date 31 October 2026. Dates ISO; INR. Amounts are outstanding invoice totals, not taxable values. All invoices are unpaid. Bank 25,000; unavoidable seven-day outflows 45,000. Beacon disputes 5,000 within F02. No credit note has yet been approved in version 1. Contacts are role labels only.

sources.title: Case G CRM release
sources.description: Use in Session 15 and capstone discovery. As-of date 31 October 2026. One row per distinct enquiry; no duplicates. Won and Lost are closed stages; Open remains undecided. Due dates refer to the next follow-up. There is no verified join key to Case F customers or invoices. Names below are fictional role owners.

extras: Client brief: The fictional Vayentra Labs founder needs a repeatable receivables-ageing model, seven-day cash view, dispute queue and handover. Start from Case F version 1. All four invoices must appear once. Due-today invoices are Current. A new as-of date must refresh buckets. Duplicates and blank amounts must trigger review. No valid join connects Case F invoices to Case G leads.

Project scope: up to six extra individual hours. Deadline is ten working days after Session 17, as confirmed by faculty. Draft recommendations only. Preserve version 1; apply the approved credit and deferral only in Session 20. Never import the separate Practice 03 receipt into this capstone.
ai: From these simulated client notes, separate stated facts, opinions, assumptions and unanswered questions. Suggest eight non-leading discovery questions. Do not create data relationships or claim an impact that has not been measured.
stretch: Explain how a genuine live project could use the same acceptance tests without exposing client identities in a public portfolio.

title: Solution Design and Project Planning
outcome: Select a feasible solution; assign tasks, effort, dependencies and testable acceptance criteria.
case: The capstone must be completed within ten working days using no more than six additional student hours each. The minimum output is a reviewed ageing queue, seven-day cash scenario, exception log and owner handover. No production system write is authorised.
concept: Acceptance criteria must be testable. A project plan links tasks, dependencies, owners and review dates. Scope decisions protect the quality of core work. A prototype can demonstrate usefulness without claiming realised impact.
example: Acceptance criterion: All four Case F invoices appear exactly once; outstanding total equals INR 100,000; overdue buckets reconcile; disputed value is shown separately as a subset.
task: Compare a spreadsheet and a slide-only solution. Select one, define five acceptance tests and build a ten-day task plan with estimates totalling no more than six hours per student.
squad: Hold a scope review. The client requests automatic payment reminders; decide whether to include draft generation, manual approval or external sending.

sources.title: Case F Receivables and cash release
sources.description: Use in Sessions 12 and 17-20. As-of date 31 October 2026. Dates ISO; INR. Amounts are outstanding invoice totals, not taxable values. All invoices are unpaid. Bank 25,000; unavoidable seven-day outflows 45,000. Beacon disputes 5,000 within F02. No credit note has yet been approved in version 1. Contacts are role labels only.

extras: Client brief: The fictional Vayentra Labs founder needs a repeatable receivables-ageing model, seven-day cash view, dispute queue and handover. Start from Case F version 1. All four invoices must appear once. Due-today invoices are Current. A new as-of date must refresh buckets. Duplicates and blank amounts must trigger review. No valid join connects Case F invoices to Case G leads.

Project scope: up to six extra individual hours. Deadline is ten working days after Session 17, as confirmed by faculty. Draft recommendations only. Preserve version 1; apply the approved credit and deferral only in Session 20. Never import the separate Practice 03 receipt into this capstone.
ai: Compare a spreadsheet and slide-only solution against the supplied capstone acceptance criteria. Propose a task plan within six additional hours per student, including testing and handover. Flag assumptions and dependencies. Do not add automated external messaging.
stretch: Write a change rule that requires re-estimation and client approval when a new data source is introduced.

title: Project Execution and Quality Assurance
outcome: Build the approved solution; test normal and error cases; record individual contributions.
case: Build the approved capstone using Case F and the client brief. Preserve the raw table and make the as-of date an input. A reviewer will test dates, duplicate records and missing amounts.
concept: Quality assurance checks normal and failure cases. A test record states input, expected result, actual result and verdict. An exception should remain visible, with a route for resolution.
example: Boundary test: invoice due on the as-of date belongs in Current, not 1-30. Changing the as-of date by one day should move it to 1-30 while preserving the total outstanding.
task: Build version 1 and execute all five acceptance tests. Keep an individual contribution log and retain one before-and-after correction. Write a short handover explaining inputs and refresh steps.
squad: Exchange files with a second squad. The receiving squad must reproduce the total and identify the stop condition without verbal help from the builder.

title: Management Review and Change Control
outcome: Present the prototype, assess an approved change and revise outputs with a clear audit trail.
case: For the capstone, management now approves an INR 5,000 credit note against Beacon invoice F02 and a rescheduling of INR 8,000 supplier payment beyond the next seven days. These are approved case instructions; no customer cash has been received. The as-of date stays 31 October.
concept: A change request records authority, reason, affected outputs and retests. A credit note reduces the receivable; it does not collect cash. A payment deferral changes the forecast timing, not the historical expense automatically.
example: If a 12,000 debtor balance receives an approved 2,000 credit note, outstanding becomes 10,000 and bank is unchanged.
task: Prepare a change-impact note and version 2. Recalculate totals, affected buckets and the seven-day cash gap. Retest all unchanged controls and issue a concise manager update.
squad: Client asks you to delete version 1 to avoid confusion. Explain the version record and publish a clearly labelled final file while preserving the original. Launch Independent Practice 5.

practice.title: Controlled change delivery
practice.brief: Apply only the Session 20 approved credit note 5,000 and supplier deferral 8,000 to Case F version 1. Do not carry across Practice 03 collection; that was a separate variant.
practice.output: Submit version 2, linked approval note, changed-output list, five regression tests and a 90-word update. State explicitly that no new cash was collected.
practice.rubric: Changed balances and gap 4; version and approval trail 2; tests 2; clear status and limitations 2.

title: Resume and Portfolio Development
outcome: Translate assessed work into credible achievements and assemble an evidence-linked portfolio.
case: A student writes: Finance expert who improved company profit 40% and managed real corporate accounts. Their evidence is a supervised simulation with no measured live profit impact.
concept: A credible achievement names the task, method, scale, result and context. Simulation work is valuable when described honestly. Different roles need different evidence selections, not inflated titles.
example: Better: Built a simulated four-account ageing model, reconciled INR 100,000 outstanding and corrected a due-date classification error; workbook and test log available.
task: Write three evidence-backed resume bullets, a 90-word professional summary and a portfolio index linking six actual outputs. Identify one skill gap for your target role and a specific practice task.
squad: Run a 45-second recruiter review. Partner chooses one claim and asks to see the calculation or work log immediately.
ai: Convert these verified evidence records into three resume bullets. Preserve the simulated or supervised context, individual contribution and measured result. Do not invent employers, certifications, experience, savings or hiring outcomes. Identify claims that need evidence.
stretch: Adapt one achievement for Accounts Assistant and MIS Trainee without changing the underlying facts.

title: Hiring Simulation and Exit Assessment
outcome: Complete an independent practical assessment and demonstrate reasoning in a structured interview.
case: You have 60 minutes for the unseen individual Exit B assessment in the handbook. The facilitator distributes it at the start. After submission, explain one correction from your portfolio in a three-minute structured interview.
concept: A practical interview tests execution and reasoning under clear constraints. Ask essential clarification questions, show workings and label uncertainty. Strong candidates explain limitations without pretending to know.
example: Interview structure: situation, your task, action, result and verification. State which part was yours and what the reviewer changed.
task: Complete the timed exit task without AI or help. Then answer: Which error did you find? How did you verify it? What would you do if a manager asked you to hide it? Record a 30-day improvement plan after feedback.
squad: Practise interviews only after all individual scripts are collected. Rotate interviewer and candidate; use evidence, not fluency or accent, as the basis of feedback.
extras: The faculty member issues the unseen 60-minute exit assessment separately. No AI or peer help during that test or your interview. This public pack contains the interview and development worksheets only.
stretch: Explain an unfamiliar discrepancy by stating a safe next diagnostic step rather than guessing an answer.

title: Corporate Presentation Preparation
outcome: Rehearse the business demonstration, defend recommendations and complete the evidence review.
case: Your squad receives seven minutes to present, three minutes for a working demonstration within that seven, then eight minutes of questions. A business reviewer needs to decide whether the output can be used under supervision.
concept: A strong demonstration shows a decision, input, check, output and limitation. A tested artifact is more persuasive than feature lists. Every team member must own a defensible contribution.
example: A seven-minute structure: problem 1 minute; evidence 1; demonstration 3; recommendation 1; limitations and next step 1.
task: Prepare up to six slides and a one-page executive summary. Run a live refresh, check all portfolio permissions and rehearse answers to three challenge questions.
squad: Peer reviewers ask: What happens if a date is blank? Which result changed after feedback? What value is measured versus proposed? Record one correction before the final submission lock.

title: Corporate Demo Day and Industry Passport
outcome: Present the project, answer reviewer questions and complete individual evidence verification.
case: The cohort presents reviewed work. Judges score independently before discussion. Each student must defend one assigned artifact and leave with a documented competence profile and next steps.
concept: A credential reports demonstrated performance within its assessment scope. Team achievement does not replace individual competence. A reviewer can recommend an improvement without claiming that a person is employable in every role.
example: A sound passport entry: Bank reconciliation - independently demonstrated on timed case; adjusted balance and timing bridge correct; evidence ID EXIT-B-02; reviewer and date recorded.
task: Present and respond to questions. Complete a 90-day plan with three actions, due dates and evidence. Audit the passport for correct identity, artifact links, scoring and limitations before acknowledgement.
squad: All students receive a two-minute individual defence station. Judges ask one question tied to the student contribution log; coordinator records feedback and unresolved evidence.
